status: CANDIDATE ANALOG CELL; NOT SELECTED, NOT IMPLEMENTED, NOT ENERGIZABLE
scope: One precision output derived from issue 58; no installed BOM, board, source epoch or population change

ports.SIGNAL: Existing local precision signal, +/-5 V; its upstream source and partial-power behavior remain a separate obligation
ports.JACK: External tip, normal +/-5 V into >=10 kohm and <=5 nF; sustained external +/-12 V fault
ports.VP: Local positive supply, 11.53..12.48 V relative to intact local GND
ports.VN: Local negative supply, -12.37..-11.74 V relative to intact local GND
ports.GND: Local analog reference; loss is explicitly considered, not assumed intact
ports.PERMIT_I_PLUS: Independent current-source port: 5 mA through both series LEDs during enabled characterization; compliance >=3.4 V at 25 C
ports.PERMIT_I_MINUS: Return to independent permit domain, never tied to local GND; disabled LED current must be 0 for the sourced off-leakage condition

replication_screen.scope: Sensitivity only, copied from issue 58 channel counts and original supply contract; not a new population or power allocation

open_obligations: Permit source, all three rail/reference qualification, and independently observable local-GND continuity are not captured; series LEDs do not detect a fault.
A voltage-only GND monitor cannot distinguish a failed return bridged by an equally low-impedance alternate return; define the monitored conductor and fault coverage explicitly.
No maximum relay leakage, resistance, contact capacitance or turnoff delay over the complete 15..30 C installation is established by the 25 C electrical table.
Determine contact voltage under whole-board floating and partial-power faults. The isolated cell alone provides no absolute bound on local common-mode voltage.
Bleeder calculation covers only two relay leakage paths into a local rail, with no other energizing port; all shared-rail injection paths and distributed capacitance require an aggregate proof.
The relay offers no overcurrent trip. Sustained enabled contention, detection plus turnoff energy, amplifier saturation/recovery and simultaneous package faults need physical qualification.

Cold/partial rail collapse leaves closed contacts conducting until detection plus actual relay release. Local reachable reservoir and powered-off amplifier output injection limit are unknown; 100 kohm leakage bleeders do not absorb this transient.
Supply bypass network, PCB clearance/footprint, installed thermal resistance and mechanical fit are not captured in this analog candidate.

Absolute calibrated accuracy at actual +/-12 V rails and installed temperatures, switching skew, off-contact capacitive injection, hot leakage and disabled output settling require evidence and bench results.
No board population or power-ledger substitution is authorized by this candidate; supply rails keep their original current and 40 mV limits.
